subject: Design: sidecar bootstrap + cert provisioning for private aliases
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: 
Date: 2026-12-10T15:03:00-08:00
Subject: Design: sidecar bootstrap + cert provisioning for private aliases

Hi team,

Sharing a proposed pattern for on-prem / VPC private endpoint certificate provisioning that Acme Health asked for during last week's call. Goal is zero-touch sidecar bootstrap that issues short-lived certs for private FQDN aliases (internal.example.acme) without exposing private CAs externally. High-level constraints from Acme:
- Customer manages DNS for their private zones (split-horizon)
- No cross-tenant CA private key sharing; they require an auditable signing flow
- Prefer short TTL certs (12h–24h) and automated rotation

Proposed approach:
1) Sidecar agent (runs in customer cluster) generates keypair + CSR locally and stores private key in local K8s secret or HSM.
2) Agent calls Redwood CA Agent (outbound-to-controlplane over mTLS) to request ephemeral signed cert. Request includes CSR and a one-time attestation token (nonce signed by customer's KMS/HSM) for identity proof.
3) Redwood CA Agent validates attestation, issues short-lived cert signed by a per-customer subordinate CA (we keep root offline). Cert includes SANs for customer-private FQDNs and a fixed SAN pattern  (*.redwood-private.acme).
4) Sidecar writes cert to node and signals runtime. All traffic to private endpoints terminates at the service using the sidecar cert.

DNS mapping and split-horizon notes:
- Customers will continue to own private DNS; we recommend they create CNAMEs from their private alias to the provided private endpoint hostname (host.redwood.internal-<id>.local).
- TTL guidance: keep A/CNAME TTLs low (60–300s) for quicker swapovers during failover.

Security controls / auditability:
- Every issue/renewal is logged to the customer's audit stream (control plane event + signed issuance record).
- Support CRL/OCSP for longer-lived certs but prefer short-lived to avoid revocation pain.

I've attached a flow diagram and a CSR template. Please review for gaps—Connor, can you call out runtime impacts / caching concerns? Marcus, any objections on SAN patterns and subordinate CA per-customer? Laura, please confirm compliance needs for audit records.

Thanks,
Kim

--
Kimberly Park
Director, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-10T17:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Design: sidecar bootstrap + cert provisioning for private aliases

Thanks Kim — overall this looks sensible. A few runtime notes from the serving/runtime side:

- KV cache: short-lived certs are fine but we need to ensure connection reuse doesn't break on rotation. Recommend a staggered renewal where sidecar requests new cert at 60–70% of lifetime and performs an in-process key swap.
- Batching: issuing many certs at the same second could spike control-plane load. Add jitter and rate-limits to sidecar (exponential backoff and windowed issuance).
- SAN patterns: avoid wildcard in SAN plus explicit hostnames; some client stacks reject wildcards for mTLS client certs. If we need a wildcard for internal aliasing, document fallback to explicit list when possible.

Small ask: add a TLS negotiation compatibility matrix for common client stacks (curl, jdk11, go1.21, python3.11). I'll draft.

-Connor

--
Connor O'Brien
Principal SRE, Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-11T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Design: sidecar bootstrap + cert provisioning for private aliases

Kim — agree with the per-customer subordinate CA; one thing to call out:

- Operations: we'll need an automated subordinate CA provisioning workflow (HSM-backed) and a rotation plan for the subordinate CA cert itself. Recommend a 2–3 year validity with annual automatic re-issuance and a documented emergency rotation playbook.
- OCSP responders: short-lived certs reduce OCSP dependence, but customers in regulated industries (like Acme) may ask for stapling evidence. We should include an optional stapling endpoint (read-only) that sidecars can query to attach stapled OCSP responses.
- CRL distribution points on private networks are painful; prefer OCSP stapling + short-lived certs.

Also, the SAN namespace that Kim suggested ( *.redwood-private.acme ) sounds fine if Acme consents; we should avoid mixing customer-controlled DNS names and our internal hostnames in one cert to minimize exposure. Propose we keep a separate internal alias and require a CNAME from the customer's private alias instead.

Marcus

--
Marcus Lin
Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Andrew Johnson <andrew.johnson@acmehealth.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: sec-acct@acmehealth.com
Date: 2026-12-11T13:44:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Design: sidecar bootstrap + cert provisioning for private aliases

Hi Kim,

Thanks for the design. A few clarifications from Acme Security:

1) Attestation token: our preference is an HSM-signed nonce; can the sidecar present a TPM/EK-based attestation instead (we run on a mix of cloud and on-prem hardware)?
2) Logging: we need per-issuance signed logs that we can ingest into our SIEM (Splunk). Can the issuance record be pushed to a customer-controlled S3 (or SFTP) endpoint?
3) SANs: we cannot have our private DNS entries present in any public certificate. Confirm subordinate CA issuance will only produce certs scoped to private namespaces and the chain will not be exported.

If those three are okay, we can proceed to a pilot next week.

Andrew

--
Andrew Johnson
Head of Platform Security
Acme Health

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: andrew.johnson@acmehealth.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-12T11:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Design: sidecar bootstrap + cert provisioning for private aliases

Andrew — thanks for the quick review. Responses inline and next steps below.

1) Attestation token: yes — sidecar will support multiple attestation mechanisms (HSM TPM attestation, KMS-signed nonce). We'll provide reference implementations for TPM and AWS Nitro/HSM flows. We'll also support customer-supplied attestation endpoints.
2) Logging: we'll publish signed issuance records (JSON lines) to a configurable sink. Supported sinks: customer S3, customer SFTP, or push to customer SIEM via HTTPS with mTLS. Records will be GPG-signed for non-repudiation.
3) SANs and chain: confirmed — subordinate CA is per-customer and the certs will contain only private namespaces. The subordinate CA private key stays in our HSM; we will not export private keys. We will provide an audit package for the pilot.

Action items / timeline:
- Connor: draft TLS compatibility matrix and renewal jitter strategy (due 2026-12-14)
- Marcus: outline subordinate CA lifecycle and emergency rotation playbook (due 2026-12-15)
- Laura: list of compliance artifacts Acme expects for the pilot (due 2026-12-14)
- Kim: schedule pilot kickoff with Acme for 2026-12-19

I'll attach the pilot checklist to the kickoff invite.

Thanks,
Kim

--

Director, Customer Solutions
